question: The two maps show the development of Shalton village between 1910 and 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
essay:
The maps illustrate how Shalton village changed over a 100-year period from 1910 to 2010. 
Overall, the village got a lot bigger and became much more developed, with loads of new residential buildings replacing traditional local shops and green spaces. 
In 1910, a large house with trees occupied the central plot enclosed by School Road, London Road, and High Street. By 2010, the big house was knocked down to make space for a cluster of new houses and a small access road. Furthermore, the grocer and baker on High Street vanished, replaced by a café, while the number of houses along the south side of High Street doubled. 
Across School Road, the butcher was replaced by a supermarket and a parking space, with a new bank built further north. On the east side of London Road, where only the post office stood in 1910, a bunch of new homes were erected. Finally, the school in the southwest corner stayed pretty much the same throughout the century.

expected.reference: Overall, the village got a lot bigger and became much more developed, with loads of new residential buildings replacing traditional local shops and green spaces.
